//: Server-side config store: API configs, connectors and the fetcher plan. Week 1 is structure only
//keys: A key starting with // is a comment; the loader skips it. A '//calls' block holds a fetcher's planned calls - inert until the prefix is dropped. 'env:NAME' is read from the environment at call time, never a committed secret. {{ ... }} tokens are substituted at call time. status: stub | planned | blocked | live.

llm_backends.//: Chatbot runs locally, so Ollama is the only AI backend. Reached over its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so llm_providers/openai_compatible.py serves it.
llm_backends.//migration: Currently built in config.py from OLLAMA_BASE_URL / OLLAMA_MODEL.

agents.//: Three agents, one backend, a separate system prompt each - routing, judging evidence and explaining someone else's output are different jobs. Prompts live with the agent code; only selection and sampling are config.
agents.job: Scope gating, request-type classification, input extraction, deciding what downstream work is needed.
agents.//detector_visibility: Reads only required_input_type and detector_configured. Never auth/request/response_mapping, never branches on mode; its output has no mode field.

agents.job: Judges scam_check from AddressContext when no detector is configured. Returns detection and explanation together, so the Forensic Investigator never runs here.
Explains a configured detector's evidence in plain language. Runs only when a detector is configured and is_llm_based is false.
agents.//faithfulness: Translation, not a second opinion. It must not re-judge, so a wrong value_map below becomes a confidently wrong explanation.

//active_detector: null = none configured, so scam_check falls through to the Scam Checker. That is what agents/business_analyser.py hardcodes today. Set to an id below to flip detector_configured true.

detectors.name: RektRadar
detectors.//timeout: Connector's job, not the mapping layer's. Timeouts and 4xx/5xx fail the same way, without running any mapping.
detectors.//auth: Free tier is anonymous and needs no key (data is ~10 min behind). optional: true sends the key when REKTRADAR_API_KEY is set and calls anonymously when it isn't.

label.//: Score is numeric, not a word, so ranges derive the enum; first match wins. Fallback covers 40-69 and flags containing insufficient_data.

confidence.//: score is a 0-100 risk, so 'risk' turns it into confidence in the label: scam = score, not_scam = 100 - score. Present-but-non-numeric is a MappingError, not a silent default.

evidence.//: Unknown code -> {description: raw code, weight: default_weight}.

codes.//source: Descriptions are RektRadar's own one-line summary from https://rektradar.io/signals/<code>/
codes.//catalog: Holds every flag seen in live replies plus every danger and good flag in the catalog. Its other warning/info flags are left out on purpose - an unknown code still shows as the raw code at default_weight.

balance_zeroing_function.description: A public function writes zero (or subtracts) directly into holder balances.

blacklisted_cluster.description: The deployer's cluster has already been flagged for producing confirmed scams.

extreme_sell_fee.description: Sell fee above 50% - borderline honeypot, the contract drains exits.

honeypot.description: The token can be bought but cannot be sold - funds are trapped on-chain.

impersonates_major_token.description: The contract spoofs the name or symbol of USDT, USDC, WETH or another major token at a fake address.

known_scam_bytecode.description: The contract's bytecode is byte-identical to a confirmed mass-scam factory RektRadar has already flagged thousands of times.

liquidity_decreased.description: More than 80% of the pair's WETH liquidity has been pulled since the initial analysis.

multi_flag_confirmed_scam.description: Both rug-setup and malicious-contract evidence are present - a near-certain scam.

multi_flag_malicious_contract.description: Two or more distinct malicious code patterns were found in the contract source or bytecode.

router_gated_balance_access.description: Balance accounting branches on the router/pair address - sells behave differently than buys.

selfdestruct_create2_combo.description: The contract can both self-destruct and redeploy to the same address - a metamorphic rug primitive.

sell_failed.description: Buy succeeds but sell reverts - classic honeypot signature.

serial_scammer.description: The deployer has multiple confirmed scam deploys - a known bad actor.

balance_manipulation.description: The owner can directly rewrite arbitrary balances (setBalance-style functions).

deploys_scam_bytecode.description: The deployer has a history of shipping contracts whose bytecode matches confirmed scams.

previous_scam_tokens.description: The deployer has previously deployed tokens that RektRadar flagged as scams.

self_destruct.description: The contract can selfdestruct - the token code can be erased from the chain.

serial_scammer_network.description: The deployer is funded by, or funds, a known serial scammer - guilt by graph association.

approve_with_transfer.description: The approve function also moves tokens - approvals should never transfer.

blacklist_detected.description: The contract can blacklist any address from selling - a kill-list with no notice period.

buy_only_pattern.description: On-chain history shows hundreds of buys and zero sells - telltale honeypot trace.

commented_renounce.description: The renounceOwnership function is commented out in the source - renouncing was never an option.

extreme_hardcoded_sell_fee.description: The verified source hardcodes a near-total sell tax (90%+), so selling burns almost the entire position.

fee_changed_post_launch.description: Fee-update events fired after the initial analysis - launch taxes were a costume.

hardcoded_address_blacklist.description: The transfer path reverts for specific addresses baked into the code.

hidden_owner.description: The source keeps an owner address in a private variable - control survives a fake ownership renounce.

liquidity_removed.description: Post-launch monitoring saw the pair's liquidity drop to zero - the rug has happened.

mass_deployer.description: The wallet has deployed 200+ contracts - almost certainly an automated scam factory.

mass_hardcoded_blacklist.description: The transfer path embeds many literal addresses followed by a revert - a baked-in ban list.

mixer_funded.description: The deployer's ETH was sourced from Tornado Cash or another mixer.

multi_flag_rug_setup.description: Three or more independent rug-pull ingredients fired on the same token at once.

ownership_reclaimed.description: Ownership was renounced... then transferred back to a live address.

proxy_implementation_known_scam.description: The implementation behind the proxy is byte-identical to a confirmed mass-scam factory.

proxy_implementation_missing.description: The proxy delegatecalls into an address that currently holds no code - a trap or a not-yet-set logic.

reentrancy_risk.description: External value calls happen before balance updates - the classic reentrancy shape.

sell_blocked.description: Sells revert with an explicit guard - not a slippage issue, an intent.

slow_rug_detected.description: Liquidity has been drained gradually - over half the peak WETH reserve is gone.

supply_inflated.description: totalSupply grew more than 10% since the analysis - someone is minting.

trading_paused_post_launch.description: The contract reports paused = true after launch - all exits are currently frozen.

tx_origin_msg_sender_check.description: The contract explicitly blocks contract callers by requiring tx.origin to equal msg.sender.

creator_holds_all_lp.description: The deployer wallet still owns 95%+ of the LP tokens - a one-tx rug is one click away.

name_mimics_known_token.description: The name or symbol matches a popular token, but the contract address is different.

opcode_selfdestruct.description: The contract can destroy itself, wiping its code and (with CREATE2) reincarnating as something else.

scam_factory_name.description: The contract's internal name matches a template churned out by a known scam factory.

single_holder_above_90pct.description: One wallet holds over 90% of the supply - total control of the float.

single_mint_concentrated.description: All tokens were minted in one transaction to a single wallet - no fair launch.

unrestricted_mint.description: A public mint() with no access guard - the supply can be inflated at will.

amount_dependent.description: Selling small amounts works, large amounts fail - partial honeypot.

dynamic_fee_by_block.description: Fees are computed from block.number or block.timestamp - taxes change on their own.

high_sell_fee.description: Sell fee in the 30-50% range - soft rug, exits are economically unviable.

misspelled_drain_function.description: A typo-named clone of approve/transfer (approvve, tranfer...) touches balances.

name_contains_url.description: The token's on-chain name or symbol carries a website, domain or claim-channel link - a phishing-bait token.

permit_abuse.description: The permit() implementation transfers tokens instead of just approving.

scam_factory_funder.description: The funder has previously bankrolled multiple scam deploys - it's a scam-factory bank.

sybil_funded_holders.description: Multiple top holders were funded by the same non-exchange wallet - fake demand, not real holders.

buy_failed.description: Even buying the token fails in simulation - likely paused or pre-launch.

lp_in_pullable_custody.description: The LP sits in a contract that looks like a lock but can release it on demand - a fake lock, not protection.

possible_simulation_detection.description: The contract reads block/miner fields that scams use to behave differently inside a simulator.

blacklist_function.description: The contract ships a function to ban specific addresses from trading.

conditional_transfer.description: The transfer path branches on block.number, block.timestamp or tx.gasprice.

lp_not_locked.description: Nothing protects the liquidity: the LP is neither burned nor held by a known locker contract.

very_few_holders.description: The token has fewer than 5 unique holders - almost no real distribution yet.

liquidity_at_creation.description: The deployer provided the initial liquidity in the same transaction as the deployment.

new_wallet.description: The deployer's wallet is less than 7 days old - disposable identity.

suspicious_selectors.description: The bytecode exposes function selectors known to enable rugs (sweepETH, removeLiquidityNoFee, etc.).

top3_hold_95pct.description: The three largest wallets control more than 95% of the supply.

block_dependent_logic.description: Behavior changes past a block number or timestamp comparison.

low_liquidity.description: The pool holds very little WETH - slippage explodes on any non-trivial trade.

mass_funder.description: The wallet that funded this deployer has bankrolled many other deployers - a scam-funding hub.

no_renounce_ownership.description: The contract still has an owner - nothing prevents a future privileged change.

single_holder_above_70pct.description: One wallet (excluding the pair) holds more than 70% of the supply.

no_dex_pair.description: The token has no liquidity pool - it cannot be traded on any DEX.

upgradeable_proxy.description: The contract can delegate or upgrade its logic (delegatecall / upgradeTo).

cooldown_mechanism.description: Per-address cooldowns restrict how often a wallet can trade.

opcode_gasprice.description: The contract reads the transaction gas price, sometimes used for anti-bot or anti-simulation logic.

trading_control.description: The contract has an on/off switch for trading (enableTrading / openTrading).

young_wallet.description: The deployer's wallet is 7-30 days old - a softer version of a brand-new wallet.

insufficient_data.description: RektRadar couldn't gather enough on-chain data to judge this token - a low score here means 'unknown', not 'safe'.

no_graph_data.description: The deployer has no funding-graph history - the wallet's origins cannot be traced.

normal_fees.description: Fees are within normal Uniswap range - neutral signal, no specific risk.

unverified_bytecode_analyzed.description: No verified source on Etherscan - analysis falls back to bytecode-only signals.

lp_burned.description: LP tokens were sent to a burn address - liquidity is locked forever, no rug from here.

lp_locked.description: LP tokens are held in a recognized lock contract for a fixed duration.

codes.//not_in_catalog: Seen in live replies but missing from rektradar.io/signals/, so the wording is our reading of the code name.

whitelisted.description: RektRadar lists this as a known, established token.

unverified_contract.description: The contract's source code isn't verified, so it can't be read publicly.

unverified_implementation.description: The upgradeable contract's real logic isn't verified, so it can't be read publicly.

v4_hook_swap_delta.description: Its Uniswap v4 pool hook can change swap amounts, so trades may not go through at the expected price.

v4_single_use_hook.description: Its Uniswap v4 pool uses a custom hook made just for this token.

network_pending.description: RektRadar's wallet-network analysis for this token is still pending.

v4_pool_found.description: It trades in a Uniswap v4 pool.

response_mapping.//risk_type: Unmapped on purpose - RektRadar has no category field, so it stays null rather than guessed. Documented limitation.

detectors.//field_test: Free-tier evaluation: a fake or malformed address returns a normal low-risk result scoring 0 with NO error, so validate address format before calling or a fake address reads as safe. Score alone is not enough; read flags too. The API's own confidence field was 0 even on a clear scam, hence confidence is derived from score.

detectors.//no_mapping: Deliberately no request or response_mapping. The template's shared schema.py already emits DetectionResult, so the mapping layer never loads in template mode.
detectors.//endpoint: Loopback for dev. Config validation rejects non-https endpoints at save time, so the validator needs a localhost exemption or this will not save.
detectors.name: MyTemplateDetector

detectors.//: Same mapping as rektradar, so the two can't drift apart. No auth - the mock needs no key.
detectors.name: RektRadar (local mock)

detectors.//: Graph-based ML model that scores a WALLET from its transaction graph (github.com/adrian-io/ethXpose). Uses the author's free hosted app, no key; a live call took ~46s, hence the long timeout. To self-host instead, run its Docker image on port 8002 (the chat app uses 8000) and set endpoint to http://localhost:8002/api/py/classify.
detectors.name: EthXpose

label.//: fraud_probability is 0-1. The middle band is too close to call.

response_mapping.//evidence: None - the reply is a probability plus a transaction graph, with no findings to list.

detectors.//: Static source-code scan for honeypot patterns. Public Cloudflare worker (github.com/Teycir/honeypotscan), 30 requests/min per IP, no key. Only works on contracts with verified source - otherwise it answers HTTP 404.
detectors.name: HoneypotScan

label.//: It only says isHoneypot at 2+ patterns, so exactly 1 pattern reads 'safe' there. That is suspicious, not safe.

confidence.//: Already confidence in its own verdict: 95 for honeypot, 100 for safe.

evidence.//: Descriptions from HoneypotScan's own lib/pattern-explanations.ts. Weights follow its severity: critical 0.9, high 0.75, medium 0.5.

balance_tx_origin.description: balanceOf uses tx.origin to fake the balance it reports.

allowance_tx_origin.description: allowance behaves differently depending on tx.origin.

transfer_tx_origin.description: transfer checks tx.origin to selectively block transactions.

hidden_fee_taxPayer.description: A hidden _taxPayer function uses tx.origin to charge fees.

isSuper_tx_origin.description: An _isSuper function grants special privileges based on tx.origin.

tx_origin_require.description: A require statement uses tx.origin for access control.

tx_origin_if_auth.description: Authentication logic checks tx.origin in if statements.

tx_origin_mapping.description: The contract stores tx.origin values in a mapping to track callers.

sell_block_pattern.description: Logic explicitly blocks sells to certain recipients.

asymmetric_transfer_logic.description: Transfers behave differently for buys and sells.

transfer_whitelist_only.description: Transfers only work if the sender or recipient is whitelisted.

hidden_sell_tax.description: A hidden sell tax of 95-100% applies.

response_mapping.//explanation: Not mapped: its message says 'No honeypot patterns detected' even when 1 pattern was found.

detectors.//: LLM (Claude) reads the verified source and scores it. Uses the author's free hosted app (github.com/amapara27/recon-ethereum-security), no key, ~3 fresh analyses a day (cached repeats are free). Planned, not live: on 2026-10-08 both the hosted app and a local copy failed every analysis because Recon's own code passes 'temperature', which the current Anthropic SDK rejects. On an LLM failure it answers HTTP 200 with only {error}, which fails the label lookup and so reads as an unreadable reply, never a verdict.
detectors.name: Recon

label.//: safe_score is 0-100 where 100 = SAFE, so the ranges are the other way round from RektRadar.

data_sources.//: Which API backs which fetcher. Endpoints and constraints only, no credentials.
data_sources.//traps: Two response shapes: account/contract/token return status+message, proxy is JSON-RPC and returns neither, so proxy success is result-vs-error presence. Applying the status check to proxy marks good responses as failed. HTTP 200 is not data: txlist with no transactions returns status '0' / 'No transactions found', a valid empty result; getsourcecode on an unverified contract still returns status '1' / 'OK' and the only tell is SourceCode == ''.
data_sources.//api_key: In .env. Missing key must fail immediately, not continue as None.
data_sources.name: Etherscan

data_sources.//decision_needed: Open: Etherscan token search or a token list API such as CoinGecko. Best-effort by nature, so ambiguous matches are flagged, not guessed.

fetchers.//: Four context fetchers plus two resolvers. Each independently callable and independently failable, so one failure leaves the pipeline running on partial context. Each writes fetcher_provenance: which field it supplied and when.
fetchers.//invocation: Triggered conditionally by the Business Analyser, never all at once. scam_check: a resolver when raw input type does not match what is required, then context fetchers when required_input_type is address_with_context - always true on the Scam Checker path. address_info: only fetchers matching requested_fields.

//calls.//: verified_source = SourceCode != ''. Unverified returns SourceCode '' and the literal string 'Contract source code not verified' as the ABI.

Runtime, not constructor bytecode - creation bytecode is silently wrong for any contract with a constructor. is_contract is true only if code is neither 0x nor an EIP-7702 delegation (23 bytes, ef0100 + 20-byte address), which is still a wallet.

//calls.yields: hash, from, to, value, timestamp, method
//calls.//: 10,000 records per call max, so longer history needs page/offset. Zero-tx address returns status '0' / 'No transactions found' - not an error.

//calls.yields: tokenName, tokenSymbol, tokenDecimal, contractAddress - all the metadata tokens[] needs
//calls.//: No free way to list tokens held: tokeninfo is Pro, tokenbalance needs a known contract. Balance = sum incoming minus outgoing per contractAddress. That is an estimate and must be flagged as one.
Only once a specific token contract is known. Optional cross-check, not a primary call.

fetchers.//role: Resolves input, does not build context. Runs when raw_input.type is tx_hash but an address is required. Output is the address the context fetchers then run against.

//calls.//: JSON-RPC: numeric fields are hex, not the decimal strings txlist uses. Do not parse as decimal.
Only for contract-creation txs, where 'to' is null and the deployed address is the receipt's contractAddress.

fetchers.//blocked: See data_sources.token_name_source. A name matching several contracts stops the pipeline with a clarifying question; the mapping layer is never reached.

cache.//: Explorer APIs are rate limited, so results are held per address for a short TTL and follow-up turns reuse them. 5-10 min is the target; 600 is the top of it. Tune in Week 2.
